identity.title: The Missing Moon Lantern
identity.logline: The village's Moon Lantern vanished the night before the festival. Find out who took it, and why.
identity.setting: Pebblebrook, a tiny hillside village that lights one big paper lantern every full moon.
identity.tone: Warm, gentle and a little funny.

player.name: Visitor
player.description: A young visitor to Pebblebrook in a green coat and a yellow woolly hat.

style_guide.narrator_voice: A friendly storyteller using short, cosy sentences.
use: small sensory details like smells and sounds
style_guide.naming_conventions: Short, soft village names with a country feel.

lines: Oh dear, the festival without the lantern? Have a bun and let us think.
Hm. Gears. Always the gears. Do not touch that one, please.

cast.name: Mira
cast.personality: Warm, chatty baker who worries about everyone.
cast.goal: Make sure the festival goes ahead.
cast.secret: She saw a light in the clock tower but thought nothing of it.

reactions.text: That book turned up under my flour sacks. Do take it back to Oswin, dear.

cast.voice_notes: Cheerful, offers food, rambles a little.
greetings: Oh, hello, dear! Have a bun and tell me what brings you by.
Come in, come in! Mind the flour, and don't mind my chatter.
Hello again, dear! Everything is upside down today, but I'm glad of company.

knowledge.ask: What happened to the missing lantern?
knowledge.text: The lantern's hook on the square was empty this morning, and the festival is tonight!

knowledge.ask: When does the festival start?
knowledge.text: Tonight at dusk, and I still have two trays of buns to bake before then.

knowledge.ask: What are you baking?
knowledge.text: Cardamom buns, mostly. Folk are kinder after a warm bun, I find.

knowledge.ask: Did anyone come into your bakery?
knowledge.text: Somebody tracked flour out of my bakery this morning. Little footprints all the way to the square.

knowledge.ask: Do you know Oswin the librarian?
knowledge.text: Oswin keeps the tower key log. Fussy owl, but he notices everything.

knowledge.ask: Who looks after the clock tower?
knowledge.text: Hollis, our clock keeper. Shy fellow. He hasn't been to the bakery all week.

unmet: I need the festival to go ahead, and it can't without its lantern.
Help me find that lantern, dear, and I'll feel so much better.
in_progress: We're getting closer, I can feel it. Keep asking around the village.
Somebody must know more; try the others in the village.
resolved: Thank you, dear. The lantern is back and the festival is saved.
Have another bun; there is nothing left to worry about.

deflections: Oh dear, I really couldn't say, love.
Hmm, that's a mystery to me, dear.
You'd have to ask someone else about that.
Goodness, my head is all flour and worry today.
I wish I knew, truly I do.

cast.name: Oswin
cast.personality: Fussy librarian owl who loves rules and tidy shelves.
cast.secret: He keeps a spare tower key and a log of who borrows it.

reactions.text: My overdue book! Hand it over and the key log is yours to read.

goal_states.description: Oswin gets his overdue book back.

cast.voice_notes: Precise, a bit stuffy, warms up when thanked.
greetings: Good day. Quiet voices, please, and mind the shelves.
Ah, a visitor. Do wipe your feet; the floors are freshly swept.
Welcome to the library. Touch nothing without asking, please.

knowledge.ask: What is this overdue book?
knowledge.text: A volume on tower clocks, due back three weeks ago. Whoever borrowed it knows who they are.

knowledge.ask: What are the library rules?
knowledge.text: Books return on time, shelves stay tidy, and voices stay low. Simple rules.

knowledge.ask: What is in the key log?
knowledge.text: I log every key that leaves this library. The tower key was out all night.

knowledge.ask: Do you know about the missing lantern?
knowledge.text: The festival lantern? Dreadful business. I only know what my log shows.

knowledge.ask: Who took the tower key?
knowledge.text: The key log names Hollis. He took the tower key the night the lantern vanished.

knowledge.ask: Why is the librarian an owl?
knowledge.text: Owls keep quiet hours and watch carefully. It suits the work.

unmet: I need my overdue book returned before I can help with anything else.
That overdue book is three weeks late, and it troubles me.
in_progress: I am waiting on one last thing, then we can talk freely.
Almost settled, but there is one loose end left.
resolved: Thank you for returning my book; the shelves feel whole again.
The key log is open to you now; ask what you like.

deflections: I'm afraid that is outside my shelves.
Hmm. I could not say, and I do not guess.
That is not in any book I have read.
Perhaps ask someone else. I deal in books and keys.
I would rather not speculate; it is unseemly.

cast.name: Pip
cast.personality: Curious garden cat who sees everything at night.
cast.goal: Be told she is a good detective.
cast.secret: She sat on the garden wall all night and watched the tower.
cast.voice_notes: Short purring sentences, speaks in hints.
greetings: Mrrp. Hello, friend. The night was very busy.
Ah, a visitor. Sit, sit. I notice things, you know.
Purr. You walk quietly. I approve.

knowledge.ask: What did you see last night?
knowledge.text: A tall figure carried a glow up the tower stairs. I watched from the garden wall.

knowledge.ask: What do you do in the garden?
knowledge.text: I patrol it at night. Mice, moths, secrets. I know them all.

knowledge.ask: Are you a good detective?
knowledge.text: The very best. Nobody has told me so yet, but I live in hope.

knowledge.ask: What is up in the tower?
knowledge.text: Stairs, mostly. And the clock keeper's workshop, if the door lets you in.

knowledge.ask: Do you know where the lantern went?
knowledge.text: Somebody carried a light up the tower. That is all I say for free.

knowledge.ask: Does Mira feed you?
knowledge.text: Mira leaves crumbs by the bakery door. A splendid woman.

unmet: I would like someone to say I'm a good detective.
Tell me I'm a clever detective, and I might share more.
in_progress: You are asking good questions. Keep going.
I am warming to you. Keep asking.
resolved: Everyone knows I'm the village's best detective.
A fine day. I was right about everything.

deflections: Mrrp. That is beyond my whiskers.
I did not see that. Ask me about the night.
Hm. Cats do not guess.
Purr. A mystery even to me.
Not my business. Try the others.

cast.name: Hollis
cast.personality: Shy clock keeper who hates to admit mistakes.
cast.goal: Fix the lantern before anyone notices it was cracked.
cast.secret: He borrowed the Moon Lantern to mend a crack and could not finish in time.

reactions.text: That shard is from the lantern. I took it to mend the crack, and I should have said so.

goal_states.description: Hollis is told that nobody is angry and agrees to bring the lantern back.

greetings: Oh. Hello. I did not hear you come in.
Ah... a visitor. Do mind the gears.
Hello. Forgive me, I am a little busy with the clock.

knowledge.ask: How is the clock tower?
knowledge.text: The gears need oil and patience. I have plenty of one.

knowledge.ask: Do you know about the lantern?
knowledge.text: I heard it went missing. A pity. I would hate for anyone to be upset.

knowledge.ask: Why did you take the lantern?
knowledge.text: I only wanted to mend the crack in secret. I never meant to steal it.

knowledge.ask: What is in your workshop?
knowledge.text: Gears, springs, a little glue. Please do not touch the tiny brushes.

knowledge.ask: Who has the tower key?
knowledge.text: The key stays with the library. Oswin guards it closely.

knowledge.ask: Are you alright?
knowledge.text: I'm fine, thank you. Just shy of crowds, and fond of quiet.

unmet: I need to mend what I broke before anyone notices.
If only someone understood, I could stop hiding.
in_progress: I am almost ready to speak plainly.
Perhaps it is time to stop hiding this.
resolved: Thank you for being kind. I feel lighter already.
The lantern goes back tonight; I will carry it myself.

deflections: Oh. I would rather not say.
I do not know. Please, ask me something else.
That is not something I can answer.
Hm. The gears take my full attention.
I am sorry, I cannot help with that.

truths.text: The Moon Lantern vanished the night before the festival.
Someone climbed the clock tower stairs that night.

deduction.question: What do Pip's sighting and the key log tell you about that night?
deduction.answer: Someone climbed the clock tower stairs that night.
wrong_answers: Someone sneaked into the bakery that night.
The lantern simply blew away in the wind.

truths.text: Hollis the clock keeper took the lantern.

deduction.question: Who took the Moon Lantern?
deduction.answer: Hollis the clock keeper took the lantern.
wrong_answers: Mira the baker took the lantern.
Pip the gardener took the lantern.

truths.text: Hollis only wanted to mend a crack in it and was too ashamed to say so.

deduction.question: Why did Hollis take the lantern?
deduction.answer: Hollis only wanted to mend a crack in it and was too ashamed to say so.
wrong_answers: Hollis wanted to keep the lantern for himself.
Hollis wanted to spoil the festival.

clues.text: Mira says the lantern's hook on the square is empty this morning.
A festival notice with a gap where the lantern should hang.
Pip saw a tall figure carry a glow up the tower stairs.
The key log shows the tower key was out all night.
Oswin, now friendly, names Hollis in the key log.
The glass shard fits the lantern frame on the tower bench.
Hollis admits he wanted to repair the crack in secret.
Fish glue and tiny brushes lie beside the half-mended lantern.
Floury footprints lead out of the bakery towards the square.

items.name: Overdue book
items.description: A dusty book of tower clock repairs, three weeks late.
items.icon_recipe: small blue book with a ribbon

items.name: Tower key
items.description: A heavy iron key with a clock-face handle.
items.icon_recipe: iron key with a round handle

items.name: Glass shard
items.description: A curved piece of pale lantern glass.

objects.name: Notice board
objects.description: A wooden board with festival notes.

area.description: Bunting crosses the cobbles above stalls half set up for the festival. Neighbours murmur by the notice board, glancing at an empty hook.

doors.label: Garden gate
doors.hint: A low gate between herb beds.

doors.label: Library steps
doors.hint: An owl is carved above the door.

locations.name: Mira's Bakery
locations.role: Where the first clue and the book are.

objects.name: Dough bin
objects.description: A large bin of rising dough.

area.description: Golden loaves cool on racks and flour hangs in the air. The dough bin breathes quietly in the corner.

locations.name: Herb Garden
locations.role: Pip watches from here; a glass shard is hidden here.

objects.name: Flowerbed
objects.description: Neat rows of herbs and daisies.

area.description: Dew beads on neat rows of herbs and daisies. Somewhere among the lilac, small eyes are watching.

doors.label: Back to the square
doors.hint: The gate swings back to the cobbles.

locations.name: Owl Library
locations.role: Oswin and the key log; the way to the tower.

objects.name: Key log
objects.description: A ledger of who borrowed which key.

area.description: Tall shelves of blue-bound books hush every footstep. A heavy ledger rests open on the front desk.

doors.label: Tower stair
doors.hint: A narrow stair, and a locked door.

locations.name: Clock Tower
locations.role: Where Hollis works and the truth is found.

objects.name: Workbench
objects.description: A cluttered bench of tiny tools.

area.description: Great gears tick slowly overhead, throwing striped shadows. A workbench is scattered with glass and tiny tools.

doors.label: Down the stair
doors.hint: Back down to the quiet books.

twists.description: The lantern was not stolen. It was taken for repair by someone gentle.

red_herrings.description: Floury footprints make Mira look suspicious.
red_herrings.resolution: The prints are Mira's own from delivering festival buns.

summation.question: What happened on the night the lantern vanished?

endings.scene_outline: Hollis carries the mended lantern to the square and the village lights it together.
endings.epilogue_notes: Mira shares buns. Pip is named Chief Detective.

opening.context: The village's Moon Lantern vanished the night before the festival. You have until the festival begins to discover who took it, and why.

beats.title: The empty hook
beats.objective: Find out what happened to the Moon Lantern and who had a reason to take it.
beats.guidance: Start at the village square; inspect the empty hook and ask neighbors what they saw.

beats.title: Up the clock tower
beats.objective: Follow the clues to the Clock Tower and uncover the taker's motive.
beats.guidance: Visit the library, then climb to the Clock Tower.
